key_insight: A non-planar 3×3 Josephson crossbar qubit can realize flux-tunable Z3 combinatorial gauge symmetry, opening a path toward engineered gauge-theory and spin-liquid-like physics in circuit QED.
engineering_relevance: This demonstrates a new qubit geometry with richer connectivity than planar circuits, expanding the design space for scalable quantum simulators and lattice-based quantum hardware.
method: Built a non-planar 3×3 crossbar Josephson array inside a superconducting cavity.
Tuned magnetic flux to probe and control Z3 gauge symmetry and symmetry breaking.
Compared measured excitation spectra with a neural-network-generated variational quantum-state model.
evidence_signal: The observed excitation spectrum matched neural-network predictions well, and fine-structure splittings near the CGS point were consistent with weak tunneling or small symmetry-breaking imperfections.
watch_item: The fine-structure near the symmetry point suggests residual tunneling or fabrication/experimental imperfections may limit ideal symmetry protection.
paper_title: Nonplanar qubit with tunable gauge symmetry
